takeon_triangle.evidence: Transfer in the report year: the RITC of Syndicate 2255 'added £83.8m to premiums written and to claims incurred ... as at 1 January 2018' (p5, p37). The earlier diagonals are not restated to include it. Each 2011-2017 column equals the 2017 report's table (syndicate_435_2017 p37) times a near-constant factor down every row, matching retranslation 'at the December 2018 year rates' (p36): e.g. 2011 175,636->181,853 and 188,598->194,526 (x1.031-1.035); 2012 174,318->183,366 and 181,783->190,853 (x1.050-1.052); 2016 122,222->126,096 and 238,290->244,992 (x1.028-1.032). The 2011-2016 steps are +8,305, -851, +1,172, -5,623, -8,672 and +1,118 (sum -4,551); none comes near £83.8m. The table does not name the column that carries the transfer. But the '2010 and prior' gross claims reserves rise from 243,862 at 31 December 2017 (syndicate_435_2017 p37) to 358,307 (p36), +114,445, and claims outstanding due after more than five years rise from 170,081 to 290,374 (p34). That column prints '-' in every estimate row, so it is outside the figure. Syndicate 2255's own 2015 report (syndicate_2255_2015 p7-8) describes its liabilities as the RITC of 'Syndicate 1861 2008 and prior years of account' and 'the 1998 to 2001 years of Syndicate 340', legacy business that belongs before 2011. The take-on does not enter the t-2 step.

takeon_triangle.evidence: The transfer the scan found is not in the 2017 accounts. p5: 'The 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 will be reinsured to close into Syndicate 4444, effective from 1 January 2018' (p7 says 'At 31 December 2017 ... accepted'). At 31 December 2017 the syndicate still owed 'Inter-syndicate loan with Syndicate 958 48,911' (p41, p44), and its investments exclude those 'held on behalf of Syndicate 958' (p26). syndicate_4444_2018 p17 confirms 'With effect from 1 January 2018 the 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 has been reinsured to close ... 2017 comparatives for syndicate 4444 are pre the RITC', and its p42 books 'RITC received 277,329' gross in 2018. The only transfer-like addition in 2017 is note 24's gross 'Other 37,196' (p42), which syndicate_4444_2018 p42 re-presents as 2017 'RITC received 36,796'; this fits Syndicate 260's RITC accepted at 31 December 2016. At £37.2m it is under a third of the +118.224m figure, so even if it all entered the t-2 step at its reserve value it could not be more than half of it. The table (p25) does not say which column carries it. This report states no amount for the Syndicate 958 transfer.
